That is a measurement rather than an assumption, and the evidence is structural as well as visual: every English page continues on the NEXT EVEN page with no gap (p12 ends Q26 (a) at its 'OR' and p14 opens with Q26 (b); p16 ends Q29 (iii) at its 'OR' and p18 opens with the alternative (iii); p18 ends Q30 (ii)'s option graphs and p20 opens with Q30 (iii); p20 ends Q31 (b)(i)(2) and p22 opens with Q31 (b)(ii)). questions.stem:
The alternating current I in an inductor is observed to vary with time t as shown in the graph for a cycle.

Which one of the following graphs is the correct representation of wave form of voltage V with time t ?

options.label: A
options.text: a plot of V against t that rises linearly from zero at t = 0 to a peak at t = T/2 and then falls linearly back to zero at t = T, staying positive throughout

options.label: B
options.text: a plot of V against t that rises linearly from zero to a positive peak, falls linearly through zero at t = T/2 to a negative trough of the same size, and returns to zero at t = T

options.label: C
options.text: a plot of V against t that holds one constant positive value from t = 0 to t = T/2 and then one constant negative value of the same magnitude from t = T/2 to t = T

options.label: D
options.text: a plot of V against t that is a sine curve – one positive half-cycle from t = 0 to t = T/2 and one negative half-cycle from t = T/2 to t = T

questions._figure: REQUIRED – the stem's own graph carries the current waveform ('as shown in the graph') and all four options are DRAWN graphs with no text of their own. Page idx 4. questions.stem: When the resistance measured between p and n ends of a p-n junction diode is high, it can act as a/an –
questions._flag: DUAL KEY. This paper's marking scheme, Section-A row 11 (ms page idx 2), prints '(A) resistor / (C) capacitor' verbatim – two letters and no prose note – so CBSE accepted EITHER and no candidate was disadvantaged by the choice made here. Shipped as C rather than the first-printed A, following the rule in SCIENCE_ADDENDUM §2(c) that the letter which TEACHES THE SYLLABUS POINT wins: a high p-to-n resistance means the junction is reverse-biased, so its widened depletion layer sits between two conducting regions and stores charge – the junction capacitance of NCERT Ch.14, which is also the subtopic this row is filed on and the subject of this same paper's Q16. 'Resistor' merely restates the stem's own premise. This is the SAME PRINTED QUESTION as the opener 2025-55-2-1 Q12, which was adjudicated to C independently; the two sets agree. The full marking-scheme cell is preserved verbatim in _cbseVoided.

questions.stem:
(a) Define resistivity of a conductor. Discuss its dependence on temperature of the conductor and draw a plot of resistivity of copper as a function of temperature.

(ii) “A high voltage battery must have a large internal resistance.” Justify.
questions._flag: SUBTOPIC IS A THREE-WAY SPLIT, recorded so the filing is not read as careless. The marking scheme (ms page idx 6) splits the three marks as: defining resistivity 1, discussing its temperature dependence 1/2, plotting resistivity of copper against temperature 1/2, and the two internal-resistance justifications 1/2 + 1/2. So one mark is 'Drift of Electrons and Resistivity', one is 'Temperature Dependence of Resistivity' and one is 'Cells, EMF and Internal Resistance'. Filed on 'Temperature Dependence of Resistivity' because sub-part (a) – two of the three marks – turns on it and the plot is its content. All three are subtopics of Current Electricity, so nothing is mis-chaptered on any reading. SEPARATELY, an award note: the scheme adds 'Note: Full credit to be given if values are not shown on the graph.' That is CONDITIONAL on the student drawing the graph – ordinary marking latitude, not an unconditional award – so per the rule table it is recorded here and NOT in _cbseVoided.

questions.context: A parallel plate capacitor has two parallel plates which are separated by an insulating medium like air, mica, etc. When the plates are connected to the terminals of a battery, they get equal and opposite charges and an electric field is set up in between them. This electric field between the two plates depends upon the potential difference applied, the separation of the plates and nature of the medium between the plates.
questions.stem: In the above figure P, Q are the two parallel plates of a capacitor. Plate Q is at positive potential with respect to plate P. MN is an imaginary line drawn perpendicular to the plates. Which of the graphs shows correctly the variations of the magnitude of electric field strength E along the line MN ?

options.label: A
options.text: a plot of E along MN that is zero at M, rises to a single maximum midway and falls back to zero at N — a smooth arch

options.label: B
options.text: a plot of E along MN that rises steeply from M, holds one constant value over the middle stretch and falls steeply to N — a trapezium

options.label: C
options.text: a plot of E along MN that is a horizontal line at one and the same value all the way from M to N

options.label: D
options.text: a plot of E along MN that starts high near M, drops to a constant low value over the middle stretch and climbs again towards N

questions._figure: REQUIRED twice over – the stem opens 'In the above figure' and refers to a drawing that carries P, Q and MN, and all four options are DRAWN graphs with no text beyond their axis labels. Page idx 20. Read on this paper's page at 2x. STEM FIGURE, layout and labelling: two horizontal plates one above the other. The UPPER plate is a solid horizontal line with 'P' at its left end and a row of short dashes (minus signs) drawn immediately above it. The LOWER plate is a solid horizontal line with 'Q' at its left end and a row of '+' signs drawn along it. A single vertical segment joins the two plates roughly midway along their length, labelled 'N' where it meets the upper plate and 'M' where it meets the lower one – so the line MN runs from the positive plate Q upward to the plate P. OPTION GRAPHS: each is labelled E on the vertical axis with an up-arrow, and M and N at the two ends of the horizontal axis; their four shapes are described in the option texts.

(i) A thin pencil of length (f/4) is placed coinciding with the principal axis of a mirror of focal length f. The image of the pencil is real and enlarged, just touches the pencil. Calculate the magnification produced by the mirror.
(ii) A ray of light is incident on a refracting face AB of a prism ABC at an angle of \(45^\circ\). The ray emerges from face AC and the angle of deviation is \(15^\circ\). The angle of prism is \(30^\circ\). Show that the emergent ray is normal to the face AC from which it emerges out. Find the refraction index of the material of the prism.
questions._flag: SUBTOPIC IS A GENUINE TIE, recorded so nobody reads the choice as careless. Sub-part (i) is a spherical-mirror problem and sub-part (ii) is a prism problem, and this paper's marking scheme (ms page idx 12) splits the five marks almost evenly between them – 2½ for the magnification against 1½ + 1 for the prism. Filed on 'Reflection by Spherical Mirrors' because that sub-part is printed first and carries the larger share; 'Refraction Through a Prism' is equally defensible. Both are subtopics of the same chapter, so nothing is mis-chaptered either way.

questions.stem:
(i) Light consisting of two wavelengths 600 nm and 480 nm is used to obtain interference fringes in a double slit experiment. The screen is placed 1.0 m away from slits which are 1.0 nm apart.
(1) Calculate the distance of the third bright fringe on the screen from the central maximum for wavelength 600 nm.
(2) Find the least distance from the central maximum where the bright fringes due to both the wavelengths coincide.
(ii) (1) Draw the variation of intensity with angle of diffraction in single slit diffraction pattern. Write the expression for value of angle corresponding to zero intensity locations.
(2) In what way diffraction of light waves differs from diffraction of sound waves ?
questions._flag: PAPER DEFECT, transcribed AS PRINTED and not corrected. Sub-part (i) states the slit separation as '1.0 nm' where the physics plainly requires 1.0 mm. Verified on THIS paper at 4x magnification (page idx 20): the printed letter is unambiguously 'n', in the same line that correctly prints '1.0 m' for the screen distance, so it is not a rendering artefact. As printed, the third bright fringe of 600 nm lies 1800 METRES from the centre. CBSE FOLLOWED THE MISPRINT THROUGH: this paper's own marking scheme (ms page idx 14) substitutes \(d = 1 \times 10^{-9}\) m, prints '=1800m' for (i)(1) and '2400 m' for (i)(2), and issues no void and no re-key – so the official answers are the absurd ones. Flagged, not fixed; adjudication is the maintainer's call. SUBTOPIC is also a split – sub-part (i) is Young's double-slit interference and sub-part (ii) is single-slit diffraction; filed on 'Diffraction' to match the opener 2025-55-2-1 Q33b, which is the same printed question, so the two rows stay on one axis. Separately, the marking scheme's own alternative route for (i)(2) writes '(n-1) x 600 = n x 450' where 480 belongs – a slip inside the scheme, affecting no printed answer.

questions.subtopic: Electrostatic Potential due to Charges and Dipoles
questions.stem:
(i) A small conducting sphere A of radius r charged to a potential V, is enclosed by a spherical conducting shell B of radius R. If A and B are connected by a thin wire, calculate the final potential on sphere A and shell B.
(ii) Write two characteristics of equipotential surfaces. A uniform electric field of 50 NC\(^{-1}\) is set up in a region along \(+x\) axis. If the potential at the origin (0, 0) is 220 V, find the potential at a point (4m, 3m).

(i) What is difference between an open surface and a closed surface ? Draw elementary surface vector \(d\vec{S}\) for a spherical surface S.
(ii) Define electric flux through a surface. Give the significance of a Gaussian surface. A charge outside a Gaussian surface does not contribute to total electric flux through the surface. Why ?
(iii) A small spherical shell \(S_1\) has point charges \(q_1 = -3\ \mu\mathrm{C}\), \(q_2 = -2\ \mu\mathrm{C}\) and \(q_3 = 9\ \mu\mathrm{C}\) inside it. This shell is enclosed by another big spherical shell \(S_2\). A point charge Q is placed in between the two surfaces \(S_1\) and \(S_2\). If the electric flux through the surface \(S_2\) is four times the flux through surface \(S_1\), find charge Q.

(i) What is the source of force acting on a current-carrying conductor placed in a magnetic field ? Obtain the expression for force acting between two long straight parallel conductors carrying steady currents and hence define 'ampere'.
(ii) A point charge q is moving with velocity \(\vec{v}\) in a uniform magnetic field \(\vec{B}\). Find the work done by the magnetic force on the charge.
(iii) Explain the necessary conditions in which the trajectory of a charged particle is helical in a uniform magnetic field.

questions.subtopic: Torque on a Current Loop and Magnetic Dipole
questions.stem:
(i) A current carrying loop can be considered as a magnetic dipole placed along its axis. Explain.
(ii) Obtain the relation for magnetic dipole moment \(\vec{M}\) of current carrying coil. Give the direction of \(\vec{M}\).
(iii) A current carrying coil is placed in an external uniform magnetic field. The coil is free to turn in the magnetic field. What is the net force acting on the coil ? Obtain the orientation of the coil in stable equilibrium. Show that in this orientation the flux of the total field (field produced by the loop + external field) through the coil is maximum.
